subject: Career
title: The Origin Story Framework
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Origin Story Framework.

hook.text: Steve Jobs: adopted kid in a garage. Oprah: poverty to media empire. Origin stories create connection.

buildup.text: Every strong brand has an origin story — a narrative that explains why you do what you do.

discovery.text: The framework: challenge you faced → insight you gained → mission it created → where you are now.

twist.text: Your story doesn't need drama. 'I fell in love with data while solving a real problem' is compelling.

climax.text: An origin story makes you memorable. Facts inform; stories stick.

punchline.text: People remember stories. Lead with yours.

quiz.question: What's the purpose of a professional origin story?
options: To create connection and explain your mission

details.summary: An origin story explains why you do what you do by connecting a personal experience to your professional purpose. It creates emotional resonance that facts and credentials alone cannot achieve, making your brand memorable and human.
details.whyItMatters: People remember stories, not resumes. An origin story transforms you from an interchangeable professional into a person with a mission, which deepens connections and influences hiring decisions.
takeaways: Connect a formative personal experience to your professional mission
Keep the story under two minutes and practice natural delivery
Authenticity matters more than drama in an origin story

faq.question: What if your career path was not driven by a dramatic moment?
faq.answer: Origin stories do not need to be dramatic. A gradual realization, a mentor's offhand comment, or a pattern you noticed over years all work. The key is that the story explains your motivation authentically, not that it creates maximum excitement.

faq.question: Where and when should you share your professional origin story?
faq.answer: Use it when asked 'tell me about yourself,' in networking conversations, on your website or LinkedIn about section, and during keynote talks. Adapt the length to the context, from a thirty-second summary to a detailed two-minute version.
